summary: The main navigation for an agent app: a narrow column of icons that can be pinned open into a sidebar with labels. A marker slides to the open item, icons can carry a count, and agent runs in progress are listed near the bottom so people can see what is still working. The page for the open item sits beside it.
use: As the left-hand navigation of an agent app or workspace.
When screen space matters and the sidebar should fold down to icons.
When people should see which agent runs are still going from anywhere in the app.
When an item needs an unread or pending count on its icon.
features: A workspace name, detail and logo at the top, set through `workspace`.
One icon button per entry in `items`; clicking one sets `value`, slides the marker to it and calls `onValueChange`.
A `badge` count on an icon, which plays an exit animation when you clear it.
A Running section listing `runs`, each with a thinking indicator and an optional `onClick`.
A pin button that toggles `expanded` to show or hide the labels; while folded, each icon shows its label as a tooltip.
Shows your own `children` beside the rail, or the open item's name over placeholder lines.
a11y: The rail is a nav element labelled "Workspace".
Each item has its label as aria-label, and the open item has aria-current="page".
The pin button is labelled "Pin sidebar" and exposes aria-expanded.
Tooltips also open on keyboard focus.

faq.q: Does the rail bind the Cmd B shortcut for me?
faq.a: No. `shortcut` is only the text shown in the pin button's tooltip. Listen for the key yourself and set `expanded` through your own state.

faq.q: How do I clear a badge when someone opens that item?
faq.a: Handle `onValueChange`, and in the same update set that item's `badge` to 0 or leave it out. The badge plays its exit before it goes.

faq.q: How do I show agent runs that are in progress?
faq.a: Pass `runs` with a `key` and `label` for each, plus an `onClick` if a run should open something. The section hides when the list is empty.

faq.q: Can I put my own page next to the rail?
faq.a: Yes. Pass it as `children`. Without children the rail shows the open item's label over placeholder lines, which is useful for prototypes.
